quotes.text: the overall idea here is that the daemon should be able to execute any workflow from start to finish without intervention. sure there may end up being errors from time to time that require intervention but for the most part it should just work. intervention should be the exception.

fields.summary: Autonomous plan of change set 01M7NWFV: no owner interview. Material: the milestone-40 hands-off interview notes (the orchestrator's record of the owner's goal and the stopgaps it ran by hand) and a read of the code. Findings: session.message (internal/api/session_message.go) journals nothing; a plain run.resume journals nothing and a manual --retry journals the same TypeRetried as a watchdog retry; run.abandon journals a finished entry; run.approve only acts at a waiting signoff step (the workflow asking the owner); an owner-rule accept/reject journals nothing in a run; nothing detects commits on a run's branch that the run did not make (run commits carry Leaf:, Review:, Change:/Actor: trailers); rhiza run status builds RunInfo (internal/api/run.go) and rhiza daemon status builds DaemonStatusResponse with DaemonRun rows (internal/api/daemon.go). The orchestrator's later evidence names a hand rhiza run start that retried a failed run's close-out as an intervention. The milestone's measure is consecutive daemon runs finishing with zero interventions.
